articles.title: FIBA Women's World Cup 2026 Team USA: What is the United States Women's National Basketball Team roster?
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers and Breanna Stewart headline a 12-player squad chasing another gold medal in Berlin
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers and Breanna Stewart headline a 12-player squad chasing another gold medal in Berlin
articles.body:
Team USA will arrive in Berlin without A’ja Wilson or Kelsey Plum , but the United States still has the kind of roster depth that makes anything short of another gold medal feel like a disappointment.

The Americans open the 2026 FIBA Women’s Basketball World Cup against China on Friday, September 4, beginning their pursuit of a fifth consecutive title.

They have won nine of the past 12 editions of the tournament and remain the standard everyone else is trying to catch.

The final roster blends established champions such as Breanna Stewart, Chelsea Gray and Napheesa Collier with a younger group led by Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese .

Wilson and Plum were ruled out shortly before the tournament because of health reasons, leading USA Basketball to add Washington Mystics teammates Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen .

“The makeup of this roster is pretty straightforward,” USA Basketball managing director Sue Bird said. “I wanted to have a mixture of people with experience, a good mixture of people with youth.”

Bird added: “That sets us up for the future, as well. But also a team that complements each other and can go on the court and win gold. That is always the north star in all of these decisions that I've made.”

Team USA roster for 2026 FIBA Women’s World Cup

Paige Bueckers — Dallas Wings

Caitlin Clark — Indiana Fever

Chelsea Gray — Las Vegas Aces

Rhyne Howard — Atlanta Dream

Sonia Citron — Washington Mystics

Jackie Young — Las Vegas Aces

Kahleah Copper — Phoenix Mercury

Angel Reese — Atlanta Dream

Breanna Stewart — New York Liberty

Kiki Iriafen — Washington Mystics

Aliyah Boston — Indiana Fever

That construction gives Team USA considerable flexibility. Clark and Gray provide elite playmaking, Bueckers can operate on or off the ball, while Howard and Young give the Americans size and shooting in the backcourt.

Stewart and Collier bring championship experience and two-way versatility, Reese adds rebounding and physicality, and Boston gives the roster a reliable interior presence.

Team USA’s path through Berlin

The United States has been drawn into Group D with China, Italy and Czechia .

Group play runs through September 7, followed by quarterfinal qualification games on September 8 and 9. The quarterfinals take place September 10, with the semifinals scheduled for September 12 and the medal games on September 13.

The WNBA paused its season from August 31 through September 17 to accommodate the tournament.

Wilson ’s absence removes the MVP of the 2022 World Cup, but Team USA still has more high-end talent than virtually any opponent it will face.

The more interesting question is how quickly that talent comes together.

With Clark, Bueckers and Reese stepping into larger international roles alongside veterans such as Stewart, Gray and Collier , this tournament could offer both a title run and a preview of the next era of USA Basketball.

articles.title: A'ja Wilson's withdrawal from the FIBA World Cup may have a secret motive: to “steal” the MVP award from Caitlin Clark
articles.standfirst: Rachel DeMita has suggested Wilson's decision could be about preserving her body for the WNBA playoffs and another MVP campaign
articles.summary: Rachel DeMita has suggested Wilson's decision could be about preserving her body for the WNBA playoffs and another MVP campaign
articles.body:
A'ja Wilson 's decision to withdraw from Team USA's 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup squad has generated plenty of discussion, particularly because the Las Vegas Aces superstar remains in the middle of another outstanding WNBA season.

USA Basketball announced Monday that Wilson and Kelsey Plum would miss the tournament in Berlin for health reasons. Washington Mystics players Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron were subsequently added to the roster.

Plum's absence is relatively straightforward to understand. The Phoenix Mercury guard was subsequently ruled out for the remainder of the WNBA season because of a lower-leg injury after spending significant portions of the campaign dealing with physical problems.

Wilson's situation is less clear publicly, and that has opened the door to speculation about why the four-time WNBA MVP chose to remain with the Aces rather than pursue another international championship.

Rachel A. DeMita was among those to question whether there could be a strategic element to Wilson's decision.

Speaking during a recent broadcast, DeMita acknowledged that Wilson's official explanation was health-related but suggested that preserving her body for the final stretch of the WNBA campaign could have been a major consideration.

“ Kelsey Plum and A’ja Wilson have actually backed out of playing for Team USA in this FIBA World Cup,” DeMita noted. “Both of them said that the reasoning was due to health reasons.”

She then distinguished Wilson's circumstances from Plum's more visible injury situation.

“Now, A’ja, we don’t know. We haven’t seen A’ja visibly be dealing with anything, and so I personally think that A’ja’s not playing with Team USA because she wants to focus on the W season,” DeMita argued. “She wants to make sure her body is good. She doesn’t want to have to go through more wear and tear again right before the playoffs.”

That theory does not necessarily mean Wilson's decision was motivated by the desire to deny Caitlin Clark an MVP award. Rather, the implication is that Wilson may be prioritizing the individual and team goals immediately ahead of her.

Wilson has plenty to play for with the Aces

The timing is particularly significant because Wilson is attempting to accomplish something that would further cement her place among the WNBA's greatest players.

She has already won four MVP awards, including each of the last two. The official WNBA GM survey conducted before the 2026 season identified Wilson as the overwhelming preseason favorite for the award, with 60% of general managers selecting her.

Wilson has continued to justify those expectations. She is averaging 26.0 points and 9.4 rebounds per game, while also contributing 3.2 assists and maintaining an elite defensive presence.

DeMita believes the stakes extend beyond the individual award.

“I think A’ja is gunning for another MVP trophy and another Finals, like they want to go back-to-back-to-back,” DeMita claimed. “The Aces want to win again, and I don’t blame her in a sense, either.”

That argument carries some weight when considering Las Vegas' position. The Aces are firmly in the playoff picture, and Wilson's availability will be central to their attempt to make another championship run.

The WNBA's schedule has also created an unusual challenge. The regular season is paused from Aug. 31 through Sept. 16 because of the World Cup, meaning players participating for Team USA face another demanding international tournament before returning to their clubs for the final portion of the regular season and playoffs.

Wilson , meanwhile, gets an opportunity to use that period to recover rather than add several high-intensity international games to her workload.

There is also an important distinction between speculation and established fact. Neither Wilson nor USA Basketball has publicly stated that winning another WNBA MVP was the reason for her withdrawal.

The official explanation remains health-related, and reports indicate that Wilson has been carrying a significant workload this season. The Associated Press reported that she needed the opportunity to rest and prepare for the postseason after playing a major role for Las Vegas.

Team USA must now adjust without its biggest interior star

The Americans will enter the World Cup without one of the most accomplished players in international basketball. Wilson was named MVP of the 2022 World Cup and also earned the outstanding-player award at the 2024 Paris Olympics.

Her absence changes the way Team USA will play. Iriafen provides another powerful interior option, while Citron adds versatility and perimeter depth.

FIBA noted that Iriafen previously appeared for the United States during the World Cup qualifying tournament, while Citron is set to make her senior World Cup debut.

Caitlin Clark will remain one of the most closely watched players on the American roster, particularly because her presence gives the tournament another major storyline.

However, Wilson's decision should not automatically be interpreted as an attempt to influence Clark's MVP chances.

The more straightforward explanation is that Wilson has a rare opportunity to protect her body during the league's most important stretch.

For a player chasing another MVP, another championship and potentially another chapter in an already historic career, that could prove to be the most valuable use of the World Cup break.

And if Wilson returns refreshed and leads Las Vegas deep into the postseason, DeMita's theory about the bigger picture may look considerably more plausible, even if there is no evidence that Wilson's decision was specifically made to “steal” the MVP award from Clark.

articles.title: What does FIBA stand for and how many countries will participate in the Women's Basketball World Cup?
articles.standfirst: The 2026 tournament features an expanded 16-nation field in Berlin.
articles.summary: The 2026 tournament features an expanded 16-nation field in Berlin.
articles.body:
FIBA is the international governing body for basketball, but its name comes from the organization's original French title rather than its modern English name.

FIBA originally stood for Federation Internationale de Basketball Amateur , which translates to International Amateur Basketball Federation.

The organization later removed "Amateur" from its official name in 1989, becoming the International Basketball Federation, but the familiar FIBA acronym was retained.

It oversees major international basketball competitions, including the men's and women's World Cups and basketball tournaments connected with the Olympic Games.

How many teams are in the Women's Basketball World Cup?

The 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup will feature 16 national teams when it takes place in Berlin, Germany, from September 4 through September 13.

That represents an expansion from the 12 teams that competed at the previous edition in Sydney in 2022.

FIBA says the move to 16 teams reflects the increasing popularity of women's international basketball.

Germany qualified automatically as the host nation, while Australia, Belgium, Nigeria and the United States secured direct qualification by winning their respective continental championships in 2025.

The remaining places were decided through qualifying tournaments.

Which countries qualified for the 2026 World Cup?

The final field consists of Australia, Belgium, China, Czechia, France, Germany, Hungary, Italy, Japan, Korea, Mali, Nigeria, Puerto Rico, Spain, Turkiye and the United States.

Those 16 countries have been divided into four groups of four for the opening stage.

Group winners advance directly to the quarterfinals, while teams finishing second and third play an additional qualification game for a place in the last eight. The bottom team in each group is eliminated.

That expanded format means the 2026 Women's Basketball World Cup will be the largest edition since FIBA moved away from the previous 12-team format.

So while FIBA's name dates back to the organization's amateur roots, its flagship women's tournament continues to evolve, with 16 countries now competing for the world championship in Berlin.

articles.title: Paige Bueckers is accused of disrespecting the United States for her viral gesture before the World Cup
articles.standfirst: A playful Team USA video has sparked criticism of the Dallas Wings star days before her World Cup debut
articles.summary: A playful Team USA video has sparked criticism of the Dallas Wings star days before her World Cup debut
articles.body:
P aige Bueckers has found herself at the center of an unexpected controversy just days before making her FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup debut for Team USA .

The Dallas Wings guard appeared in a viral social-media video posted by Angel Reese , where several members of the American roster were dancing and joking around while wearing their Team USA jerseys.

What was intended as a lighthearted moment quickly drew criticism online, with some fans accusing Bueckers of disrespecting the national team uniform.

Bueckers became the focus of the reaction after footage showed her upside down against a wall while twerking. The clip, taken from Reese's TikTok video, spread across social media after being reposted on X by an account covering the Wings.

The reaction has centered less on what Bueckers actually did than on where she did it and what she was wearing.

Some fans argued that a Team USA jersey carries a level of symbolism that makes certain behavior inappropriate, particularly immediately before a major international tournament.

There is, however, no indication that USA Basketball has determined Bueckers violated any team rule or that officials intend to discipline her over the video.

The controversy comes at an especially prominent moment for Bueckers . The former UConn superstar is preparing to play in her first senior World Cup after helping Team USA win at the youth level.

FIBA lists Bueckers among the American players making their World Cup debut in Berlin alongside Reese and Caitlin Clark .

Team USA opens the tournament against China on Friday, Sept. 4, before facing Italy and Czechia in Group D. The Americans enter the competition chasing an unprecedented fifth consecutive World Cup championship.

That pursuit has already become more complicated.

Team USA enters the World Cup with added pressure

The Americans lost two of their biggest stars before the tournament. A'ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum withdrew because of health issues, forcing coach Kara Lawson to make changes to the roster. Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen received the call to replace them.

That leaves Bueckers with an even more important role as Team USA attempts to maintain its remarkable international dominance.

The 2026 roster was originally packed with established stars and rising talent. Alongside Bueckers , the group included Clark , Reese, Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier, Chelsea Gray, Kahleah Copper and Rhyne Howard .

The combination gave the Americans considerable experience despite the presence of several first-time World Cup players.

The timing of the social-media controversy has therefore added another storyline to an already closely watched tournament.

Bueckers and Reese have previously found themselves involved in an online controversy together. During WNBA All-Star Weekend, the pair appeared in a video discussing a joking $400 wager connected to a Wings-Dream game.

The WNBA subsequently removed the post and reminded the players that conversations about betting on league games can create problems under its gambling policies.

“If y’all win, you get your 400,” Reese appears to say before adding that if Atlanta wins, “you owe me 400.” Bueckers later appeared to feign confusion when asked about the exchange.

The league subsequently explained its decision to remove the video.

“While the social media post was intended to be lighthearted, WNBA players are well aware of the league’s policies prohibiting betting on WNBA games and receive training every year reinforcing those policies,” it read.

“We recognized that the post missed the mark, removed it shortly after it was published, and addressed the matter internally. We will also use this as an opportunity to reemphasize with the players involved that conversations about wagering on WNBA games, even when intended as a joke, can have negative consequences.”

The latest incident is considerably different. Unlike the wagering controversy, there is no indication that Bueckers broke a gambling rule or committed a violation that would trigger league discipline.

Still, the reaction highlights the unusual scrutiny surrounding Team USA athletes. Wearing the national jersey places players in a highly visible role, and fans can interpret even casual social-media moments through that lens.

Bueckers herself has already embraced the significance of representing the United States. Her selection followed an impressive rise from UConn star to WNBA standout, and she now enters her first senior World Cup alongside Clark and Reese as part of the next generation of American stars.

The U.S. also faces a more competitive international field than it has in recent years. FIBA expects France, Belgium and Spain to challenge the Americans, while Team USA's opening group includes China, Italy and Czechia.

For now, the viral clip remains a social-media controversy rather than a basketball story. There has been no public announcement of punishment, and Bueckers remains part of Lawson's roster as the Americans prepare for Friday's opener. Once the ball goes up in Berlin, the focus will quickly shift back to the court.

For Bueckers , that may be the easiest way to answer the criticism: by helping Team USA continue its pursuit of another world championship.

articles.title: When is Team USA playing in the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup?
articles.standfirst: The U.S. opens its title defense against China in Berlin before facing Italy and Czechia in group play.
articles.summary: The U.S. opens its title defense against China in Berlin before facing Italy and Czechia in group play.
articles.body:
T eam USA begins its run at the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup on Friday, Sept. 4, with a group-stage matchup against China in Berlin.

The tournament runs through Sept. 13 in Germany, bringing together 16 national teams for the biggest women's international basketball competition between the 2024 Paris Olympics and the 2028 Los Angeles Games .

All games will take place in Berlin, with action split between the 14,000-seat Berlin Arena and the 9,000-capacity Max-Schmeling-Halle.

For American viewers, every Team USA game will be available on TNT or TruTV, while all 36 games at the tournament will stream live on HBO Max. NBC Sports reports that TNT and TruTV will carry 17 games overall, including every U.S. contest.

The Americans enter the tournament with enormous expectations. Head coach Kara Lawson 's team is attempting to extend an extraordinary run of success on the international stage.

According to NBC Sports, the U.S. has won 66 consecutive games across Olympic and World Cup competition, with its last defeat coming against Russia in the 2006 World Championship semifinals.

This year's roster also brings together an intriguing mix of established veterans and some of the biggest young stars in women's basketball.

Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese headline the group, with all three entering their first major senior World Cup.

They join veterans including Breanna Stewart, Chelsea Gray, Napheesa Collier, Kahleah Copper and Jackie Young . Aliyah Boston, Rhyne Howard, Sonia Citron and Kiki Iriafen round out the 12-player roster.

Team USA's World Cup schedule and how to watch

The opening phase gives the Americans three games in four days, making the schedule a demanding early test.

Friday, Sept. 4 — USA vs. China

Team USA starts against China at 8:15 a.m. Eastern time. The game tips off at 2:15 p.m. local time in Berlin. It is the first opportunity for the new-look American group to establish its rhythm in a tournament where every game carries significance.

Sunday, Sept. 6 — USA vs. Italy

The Americans return to action two days later against Italy. The later start makes this the more convenient game for U.S. viewers, although it also gives the team less recovery time between contests.

Monday, Sept. 7 — USA vs. Czechia

The group stage concludes against Czechia on Sept. 7. The U.S. will then learn its exact route through the knockout rounds based on the final Group D standings. The official FIBA schedule lists the group phase through Sept. 7 before the tournament moves into its final stages.

The three group games are the only Team USA matchups that are currently fixed regardless of results. If the Americans advance, their schedule continues on Sept. 10 in the quarterfinals.

A quarterfinal victory would put Team USA into the semifinals on Sept. 12, followed by either the championship game or third-place game on Sept. 13. FIBA has confirmed those knockout-round dates, but the exact opponents and game slots depend on how the group and qualifying rounds play out.

That format means American fans could potentially see the U.S. play as many as six games in Berlin: three group contests, a quarterfinal, a semifinal and the championship game.

For viewers who want to follow the entire tournament rather than just Team USA, FIBA says Courtside 1891 on DAZN will provide live and on-demand coverage of every game, with English commentary and Spanish available for selected contests. FIBA also recommends checking individual game pages because broadcast partners can vary by country.

The World Cup represents another major test for a U.S. program that has dominated women's international basketball for two decades.

The tournament runs through Sept. 13 in Germany, bringing together 16 national teams for the biggest women's international basketball competition between the 2024 Paris Olympics and the 2028 Los Angeles Games .
All games will take place in Berlin, with action split between the 14,000-seat Berlin Arena and the 9,000-capacity Max-Schmeling-Halle.

For American viewers, every Team USA game will be available on TNT or TruTV, while all 36 games at the tournament will stream live on HBO Max. NBC Sports reports that TNT and TruTV will carry 17 games overall, including every U.S. contest.

According to NBC Sports, the U.S. has won 66 consecutive games across Olympic and World Cup competition, with its last defeat coming against Russia in the 2006 World Championship semifinals.
This year's roster also brings together an intriguing mix of established veterans and some of the biggest young stars in women's basketball.
Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese headline the group, with all three entering their first major senior World Cup.

The Americans return to action two days later against Italy. The later start makes this the more convenient game for U.S. viewers, although it also gives the team less recovery time between contests.

articles.title: Where to watch Team USA vs China? Time and TV channel for the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup game
articles.standfirst: Team USA faces its first Group D opponent
articles.summary: Team USA faces its first Group D opponent
articles.body:
The 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup gets underway with a high-voltage showdown. At Berlin's Max-Schmeling-Halle, the United States and China face off on the opening day of Group D, a clash that brings together two of the teams with the richest history in international women's basketball and that, from the opening tip, will set the tone for the group.

Group D is one of the strongest in the tournament. In addition to the United States and China, it is completed by Czechia and Italy, so no slip-up will come cheap. Starting with a win not only adds to the standings: it provides a psychological edge and puts either of these two powers on the direct path to the next round, in a format where six teams advance from the group stage.

The United States arrives as the mandatory benchmark of women's basketball worldwide. Its 12-player roster brings together some of the most decisive stars on the professional circuit, such as Caitlin Clark and Angel Reese.

China, for its part, comes in with a larger group —17 names in the squad— that combines veteran experience, towering height, and a new generation of talent poised to make the definitive leap.

What time is the USA vs China game in the FIBA Women's World Cup?

The appointment for the first game of the United States Women's Basketball Team is this Friday, September 4, 2026 at 8:15 a.m. Eastern Time, in an arena with a capacity of 9,000 fans.

In the rest of the United States, the game will start at:

Where can you watch Team USA's game in the United States?

The first Team USA game in the Women's Basketball World Cup can be watched live on television on the following channels and streaming services:

Team USA vs China Rosters: offensive power against an interior wall

The great appeal of the game lies in the clash of styles. The United States is betting on a roster of stars spread across every position. On the perimeter are Sabrina Ionescu, Kelsey Plum, Chelsea Gray, Jewell Loyd, and Ariel Atkins, a group of point guards and shooting guards capable of punishing from long range and creating plays.

Up front, the American squad arrives strong with Napheesa Collier, Kahleah Copper, Kiki Iriafen, Angel Reese, and Breanna Stewart. At point guard, it is locked down by Paige Bueckers, Sonia Citron, Chelsea Gray, Rhyne Howard, Jackie Young, Aliyah Boston, and Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark. It is a team built to impose tempo, run the floor, and deliver suffocating defense.

China responds with its trademark: height. In the paint, Li Yuan and Han Xu stand out, two imposing-sized centers, along with Mingling Chen, Chen Yujie, Zhang Manman, and the very young Zhang Ziyu. Playmaking falls to guards such as Wang Siyu, Yang Shuyu, and Sun Yu; at the forward positions, Xinyu Luo, Saiqi Jia, and Ziting Tang offer a balance between shooting and defensive work.

China’s approach will be to capitalize on its height advantage on the boards and slow the game down to limit the United States’ transition opportunities. The Americans’, by contrast, will be to speed things up, apply pressure, and turn every turnover into easy points.

Players to watch during the game

A'ja Wilson : a benchmark center, capable of dominating inside and out. Her direct matchup with China's height will be one of the key aspects of the game.

Breanna Stewart : a complete-profile forward, with outside shooting and presence in the paint. She is the kind of player who decides close games.

Han Xu : with her wingspan, she is the piece China will try to use to balance the scales on the boards and protect the rim against American attacks.

What's at stake in Group D for qualification

As this is the first matchday, all teams begin with a 0-0 record. However, the importance of this clash is enormous: a U.S. victory would immediately establish it as the clear favorite in Group D, while a Chinese win would be a statement victory on a global scale and a message to the rest of the contenders.

With Czechia and Italy also in the fight, the point differential that comes out of this game could prove decisive when it comes to determining positions and matchups in the following rounds.

Prediction for Team USA's first game at the 2026 FIBA World Cup

The United States starts as the clear favorite thanks to its roster depth, versatility, and accumulated experience in major tournaments. The talent spread across Ionescu, Plum, Stewart, and Wilson offers too many offensive solutions.

China has the tools to make things uncomfortable — its interior size is a real weapon — and it can keep the score close for much of the game if it controls the pace. Even so, the United States' athletic superiority and bench depth should make the difference in the final minutes.

The reasonable bet is a United States victory, with China offering resistance especially in the first half before the Americans pull away.

Whatever the outcome, Berlin will have the privilege of opening Group D with the most enticing matchup of the opening day.

articles.title: Who is Team USA's next opponent at the FIBA Women's World Cup 2026? Date and schedule for their next game
articles.standfirst: Caitlin Clark and Team USA begin their title defense against China in Berlin
articles.summary: Caitlin Clark and Team USA begin their title defense against China in Berlin
articles.body:
T eam USA 's long-awaited campaign at the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup is finally underway, with the Americans facing China in their opening game of the tournament.

The United States entered the competition as the reigning four-time world champion and is attempting to extend an extraordinary run of dominance on the international stage.

The 2026 tournament is being held in Berlin, Germany, from September 4 through September 13, with 16 national teams competing for the world championship.

For Team USA , the first assignment is China, with the Group D matchup scheduled for Friday, September 4.

FIBA lists the game for 12:15 p.m. local time in Berlin at Max-Schmeling-Halle , which translates to 6:15 a.m. Eastern Time, but the correct U.S. broadcast schedule places the tip at 8:15 a.m. ET, or 1:15 p.m. BST in the United Kingdom. CBS Sports lists TNT and HBO Max as the U.S. viewing options.

The game represents the beginning of a demanding group-stage schedule for Kara Lawson 's team.

Team USA was drawn into Group D alongside China, Italy and Czechia, meaning the Americans have three games to establish their position before the tournament moves into the knockout rounds.

China is not an opponent Team USA can afford to overlook. The Chinese national team reached the 2022 World Cup final, where it finished as runner-up to the United States.

FIBA's head-to-head record also illustrates the Americans' historical advantage, with the U.S. entering their latest meeting having won all 15 previous recorded matchups against China.

The matchup is also significant because this Team USA roster represents something of a changing era.

Caitlin Clark, Paige Bueckers and Angel Reese are among the players making their major senior international tournament debuts, while veterans such as Breanna Stewart, Napheesa Collier, Chelsea Gray and Jackie Young provide championship experience.

Team USA's road through Group D

The Americans' roster did undergo two significant changes before the tournament began. A'ja Wilson and Kelsey Plum withdrew for health reasons, with Washington Mystics players Kiki Iriafen and Sonia Citron called into the squad as replacements.

Wilson was Team USA's leading scorer at the 2024 Olympics, making her absence particularly notable, while Plum had also been an important member of recent championship teams.

Despite those changes, expectations remain extremely high. Team USA has not lost a World Cup game since falling to Russia in the 2006 semifinals and is seeking its fifth consecutive championship.

FIBA says the Americans' unbeaten run in the competition has stretched across multiple editions, while the roster combines established stars with a new generation of American talent.

Lawson has also acknowledged that the international field has become increasingly competitive.

"The world is improving and has continued to improve, and there's more depth to the teams at the World Cup now," Lawson said this week.

That makes the opening game against China an important early test, particularly for a roster that has not played together extensively at this level.

What is Team USA's next game after China?

Once the Americans complete their opening assignment, their attention will immediately turn toward Italy.

Team USA is scheduled to play Italy on Sunday, September 6, in its second Group D contest. CBS Sports lists that game for 2:45 p.m. ET, with TNT and HBO Max carrying the action in the United States.

The group stage concludes the following day when Team USA meets Czechia on Monday, September 7, also at 2:45 p.m. ET according to the CBS Sports schedule. FIBA's official schedule lists the matchup for 6:45 p.m. local time in Berlin.

The structure of the tournament means the group games carry added importance. The four group winners will advance directly to the quarterfinals, while the teams finishing second and third must go through qualification games on September 8 and 9. The bottom team in each group is eliminated.

The quarterfinals are scheduled for September 10, followed by the semifinals on September 12. The championship game and third-place game will take place on September 13 in Berlin.

For Team USA , the immediate objective is therefore straightforward: navigate China, Italy and Czechia successfully and put itself in the strongest possible position for the knockout phase.

With Clark making her World Cup debut and several other young stars taking on their first major senior tournament, the opening game against China is more than simply the first entry on the schedule.

It is the first opportunity to see whether this new-look American roster can maintain the standard established by the teams that came before it.

- Team USA vs. China: Friday, September 4, 8:15 a.m. ET / 1:15 p.m. BST

- Team USA vs. Italy: Sunday, September 6, 2:45 p.m. ET

- Team USA vs. Czechia: Monday, September 7, 2:45 p.m. ET

- Quarterfinals: Thursday, September 10

- Semifinals: Saturday, September 12

- Final: Sunday, September 13
